record.paper_title: Open Problems in the Function Theory of the Bergman Space
record.context_brief: Positivity of a singular fourth-order Green function
record.original_question: For every finite zero divisor G of the Bergman space L2_a(D), is the Green function for the singular fourth-order elliptic operator Delta |G|^{-2} Delta positive on D x D, where the Green function U_G(z, zeta) solves Delta_z |G(z)|^{-2} Delta_z U_G(z, zeta) = delta_zeta(z) in D with U_G and its boundary gradient equal to zero on the unit circle?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.1. The Green function for the singular fourth order elliptic operator Delta |G|^{-2} Delta is positive on D x D for every finite zero divisor G for the space L2_a(D).
Here we mean by the Green function the solution U_G(z, zeta) to the problem Delta_z |G(z)|^{-2} Delta_z U_G(z, zeta) = delta_zeta(z), z ∈ D.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ be the open unit disk and let $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ denote the Bergman space of holomorphic functions on $\mathbb{D}$ that are square-integrable with respect to area measure. A function $G\in L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ is called a finite zero divisor if there exists a finite set of points $\{z_1,\dots,z_n\}\subset\mathbb{D}$ (with multiplicities) such that $G$ is the (canonical) extremal solution to the problem of maximizing $\operatorname{Re} f(0)$ among functions $f\in L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ with $\|f\|_{L^2_a}\le 1$ that vanish on this set (so $G$ has unit norm and vanishes precisely on the prescribed finite zero set).

For such $G$, consider the singular fourth-order elliptic operator $\Delta\,|G(z)|^{-2}\Delta$ on $\mathbb{D}$, and let $U_G(z,\zeta)$ be the Green function of this operator under Dirichlet boundary conditions, i.e., the unique distributional solution of
$$\Delta_z igl(|G(z)|^{-2}\Delta_z U_G(z,\zeta) igr)=\delta_\zeta(z),\qquad z\in\mathbb{D},$$
with $U_G(\cdot,\zeta)=0$ and $\partial_n U_G(\cdot,\zeta)=0$ on $\partial\mathbb{D}$, for each fixed $\zeta\in\mathbb{D}$.

Prove or disprove: for every finite zero divisor $G$ of $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$, the Green function $U_G(z,\zeta)$ is nonnegative for all $(z,\zeta)\in\mathbb{D}	imes\mathbb{D}$.
artifact.category_tag: Weighted biharmonic Green functions on Bergman spaces
artifact.status_search_result: Positivity of the Green function for $\Delta w^{-1}\Delta$ on the unit disk is known in several important cases: Hedenmalm established it for radial weights of the form $(1-|z|^2)^{-\alpha}$, and Shimorin and others extended positivity results to radial, logarithmically subharmonic, area-integrable weights and to certain rational weights, including the case $w=|G|^2$ for canonical divisors of zero sets with two points (Blaschke-product type). For general finite zero divisors $G$, however, the full conjecture appears to remain unresolved in the literature, so its status is best described as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: The Green function for the weighted biharmonic operator Δ(1−|z|²)^{−α}Δ
status_evidence.snippet: An explicit integral formula is obtained for the Green function of the weighted biharmonic operator Δ(1−|z|²)^{−α}Δ in the unit disk, showing the positivity of the Green function.
status_evidence.claim: Positivity proven for radial power weights.

status_evidence.title: Weighted biharmonic Green functions for rational weights
status_evidence.snippet: For a Blaschke product with two zeros, the Green function is positive under certain conditions, and an explicit formula is obtained for the operator involving the canonical zero-divisor of a finite zero set on the Bergman space.
status_evidence.claim: Positivity verified in special finite-zero-divisor cases (two-point zero sets).

status_evidence.title: Construction of Green functions for weighted biharmonic operators
status_evidence.snippet: The Green function is nonnegative everywhere if the weight function w is radial, logarithmically subharmonic, and area integrable.
status_evidence.claim: Positivity established for radial logarithmically subharmonic weights, not for general |G|^2.
